descriptionChirho: The proper noun Yāmîn (יָמִין), meaning 'right hand' or 'south,' used for several individuals: (1) a son of Simeon (Gen 46:10; Ex 6:15; Num 26:12), (2) a son of Ram, grandson of Jerahmeel (1 Chr 2:27), and (3) a Levite who helped Ezra explain the Law to the people (Neh 8:7). English renders 'Jamin' and 'Yamin'; Spanish 'Yamín/Yamin/Jamín'; Arabic يامين/يَامِينُ (Yāmīn); Korean 야민 (Yamin); Swahili 'Yamini'; Hindi यामीन (Yāmīn). The two clusters differ only in the presence or absence of the conjunction waw and preposition lamed (and-Jamin, to-Jamin vs. Jamin), which are grammatical inflections (conjunction, prepositional government) rather than semantic distinctions. All occurrences denote the same proper name applied to different individuals.
